ओषधि: Oṣadhi f. (pl.): Plants used as missiles ? Described as ‘shining’ (दीप्यमानाः); held by Aśvinau when they got ready to strike at Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna at the Khāṇḍava forest 1. 218. 32, 37.
ओङ्कार: Oṃkāra m.: Name of the sacred syllable. Suparṇa (Garuḍa) told Gālava that in the east ओंकार was produced 1000 times (? ओंकारस्यात्र जायन्ते सूतयो दशतीर् दश) 5. 106. 14 (Nī., however, takes दशती to mean ‘one thousand’ and reads सृतयो for सूतयो; he explains the line as: दशशतीशब्दस्य पृषोदरादिशकारलोपेन दशतीशब्दः सहस्रवाची सृतयो मार्गाः । ‘ओंकारो वै सर्वा वाक्’ इति श्रुतेर् वेदस्य शाखाप्रशाखादिभेदो ऽत्रैव जात इत्य् अर्थः on Bom. Ed. 5. 108. 14); the शास्त्र that was proclaimed unanimously by the seven sages Marīci, Atri, Aṅgiras, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu and Vasiṣṭha (12. 322. 27) was at the very beginning adorned with the syllable ॐ (आदाव् एव हि तच्छास्त्रम् ओंकारस्वर-भूषितम्) 12. 322. 34; when Agni was cursed by Bhṛgu, he disappeared; then the people, since they could not give offerings in the fire became devoid of ओंकारस् and वषट्कारस् (निरोंकारवषट्काराः … विना-ग्निना प्रजाः सर्वास् तत आसन् सुदुःखिताः) 1. 7. 13.
ओघवती: Oghavatī f.: Name of a river. A. Origin: One half of the body of Oghavatī, daughter of Oghavant and wife of Sudarśana (13. 2. 37-38), became a river of that name for purifying the world; she could achieve this feat due to her austerities and her mastery over योग (एषा हि तपसा स्वेन संयुक्ता ब्रह्मवादिनी । पावनार्-थं च लोकस्य सरिच्छ्रेष्ठा भविष्यति ॥ अर्धेनौघवती नाम त्वाम् अर्धेनानु-यास्यति । शरीरेण महाभागा योगो ह्य् अस्या वशे स्थितः ॥ ) 13. 2. 82-83. B. One of the forms of Sarasvatī: One of the seven Sarasvatīs 9. 37. 4; when Sarasvatī of divine water (दिव्यतोया), invited by Vasiṣṭha, arrived at Kurukṣetra, she was known as Oghavatī 9. 37. 25. C. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhārata-varṣa; its water used by people for drinking purposes 6. 10. 21, 13; flowing near the place where Bhīṣma lay on his bed of arrows 12. 50. 6-7. D. Description: Holy (पुण्या) 9. 61. 37; the best among the rivers (सरिच्-छ्रेष्ठा) 13. 2. 82; all the rivers listed by Saṃjaya are described as mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for cita-tion see Atikṛṣṇā). E. Epic connection: (1) Bhīṣma lay on a cluster of arrows on the bank of Oghavatī on a highly religious spot (देशे परमधर्मिष्ठे) 12. 50. 7; (2) After the war was over the Pāṇḍavas, before proceeding to Hāstinapura, decided to spend a night near the river Oghavatī 9. 61. 37.
ओड्र: Oḍra1, Uḍra m. (pl.): Name of a country and its people. A. Location: In the south (प्रययौ दक्षिणां दिशम्) 2. 28. 1; (दक्षिणाभि-मुखो ययौ) 2. 28. 8: (प्रायाद् विजयी दक्षिणां दिशम्) 2. 28. 37. B. King: King of the Uḍra country referred to as Uḍrarāja (पाण्ड्योद्रराजौ) 2. 4. 21; or simply as Uḍra (यत्र सर्वान् महीपालान् … सपौण्ड्रोड्रान्) 3. 48. 18. C. Descrip-tion: (i) of the people: Live in country side (विषयवासिन्), but lead the life of Dasyus (दस्युजीविन्) 12. 65. 15; broad-chested, having long arms, very tall, pleas-ing to look at, wearing chaplets, having red teeth, walking like elephants in rut, wearing garments of different colours, smeared with fragrant powders (व्यूढो-रस्का दीर्घभुजाः प्रांशवः प्रियदर्-शनाः ॥ आपीडिनो रक्तदन्ता मत्तमातङ्ग-विक्रमाः । नानाविरागवसना गन्धचूर्-णावचूर्णिताः ॥ ) 8. 8. 15-16; (ii) of their warriors: carrying swords bound (to their waists), noose in hand, capable of resisting elephants, dying together when lined up in the front of the army, equipped with quivers full of arrows, holding bows in hands, long-haired, loving wars (बद्धा-सयः पाशहस्ता वारणप्रतिवारणाः । समानमृत्यवो राजन्न् अनीकस्थाः पर-स्परम् ॥ कलापिनश् चापहस्ता दीर्घकेशाः प्रियाहवाः । ) 8. 8. 17-18; as soldiers they received large amounts as payments (भृता वित्तेन महता) 8. 8. 15. D. Epic events: (1) The king (not named) of the Uḍra country mentioned among those who wait-ed on Yudhiṣṭhira in his newly-built Sabhā (धर्मराजम् उपासते … पाण्ड्योड्रराजौ) 2. 4. 18, 21; (2) Sahadeva, in his expedi-tion to the south, subjugated them just by sending envoys and made them pay tribute (पाण्ड्यांश् च … उड्रकेरऌऐः । … दूतैर् एव वशे चक्रे करं चैनान् अदापयत् ॥ ) 2. 28. 48-49; (3) The king of the Uḍra country mentioned among those who were frightened by the lustre of weapons; they attended the Rājasūya sacrifice of Yudhiṣṭhira and served meals (यत्र सर्वान् महीपालान् शस्त्रतेजो-भयार्दितान् । … सपौण्ड्रोड्रान् … आगतान् … यज्ञे ते परिवेषकान्) 3. 48. 18, 22; (4) Mentioned among those who, led by Bhīma and others, marched to attack the Kaurava army (अस्मान् अभ्यागमन् पार्था वृकोदर-पुरोगमाः । … पाण्ड्याश् चौड्राः) 8. 8. 13, 15. E. Past event: King Māndhātṛ once asked Indra what was the धर्म of the Oḍras and how they should be restrained by kings like him (ओड्राः … कथं धर्मं चरेयुस् ते … मद्विधैश् च कथं स्था-प्याः) 12. 65. 14-15; Indra then told him the धर्म of Dasyus 12. 65. 17-22.

Oḍra2 m. (pl.): Name of a people. A. Location: Probably they lived in the valleys in the north since they are men-tioned with other northern tribes (चीनान् हूणाञ् शकान् ओड्रान् पर्वतान्तरवासिनः) 2. 47. 19. B. Epic event: Oḍras brought tribute for Yudhiṣṭhira's Rājasūya but were not allowed to get through the gate (बलिं च कृत्स्नम् आदाय द्वारि तिष्ठन्ति वारिताः) 2. 47. 25; their tribute consisted of ten thousand tamed and famous asses having large bodies and long necks and who could walk long distances (? शतपातिनः); woolen materials, large in size, rich in colour, very soft to touch, produced in the Bāhlī and Cīna countries, also रङ्कु-hides, silk, jute (? पट्टज). other non-cotton woolen mate-rials in thousands which was bound in bundles (? कुट्टीकृतम्), soft, having the colour of lotus, and also soft deer skins (कृष्णग्रीवान् महाकायान् रासभाञ् शत-पातिनः । आहार्षुर् दशसाहस्रान् विनीतान् दिक्षु विश्रुतान् । प्रमाणरागस्पर्शाढ्यं बाह्लीचीनसमुद्भवम् । और्णं च राङ्क-वं चैव कीटजं पट्टजं तथा ॥ कुट्टि-कृतं तथैवान्यत् कमलाभं सहस्रशः श्लक्ष्णं वस्त्रम् अकार्पासम् आविकं मृदु चाजिनम् ॥ ) 2. 47. 21-23; (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 2. 51. 27: कुटीकृतम् चित्रगुच्छा-कारं कृतम्; he cites Viśva (स्यात् कुटी  … चित्रगुच्छके) for the meaning of कुटी); they also brought with them sharp, long swords, ऋष्टिस्, शक्तिस् and axes (पर-श्वधान्), sharp axes (परशून्) produced in the west (अपरान्तसमुद्भूतान्), various juices (रसान्) and perfumes (गन्धान्) as also various jewels 2. 47. 24-25 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 2. 51. 28: अपरान्तात् पश्चिम-देशात् समुद्भूतान्: on 2. 51. 29: रसान् रसवन्ति तर्बुजादीनि गन्धान् गन्धवन्ति मृगमदादीनि).
ओष्ट्र: Oṣṭra m. (pl.): Name of a people. Mentioned by Saṃjaya among the (northern) Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध गदतो मम) 6. 10. 37, 5; (ओष्ट्रा पुण्ड्राः) 6. 10. 56; in Saṃjaya's enumeration, immediately after these follow the southern Janapadas (अथापरे जन-पदा दक्षिणा भरतर्षभ) 6. 10. 56. [Identical with the next ?]
ओष्ट्रकर्णिक: Oṣṭrakarṇika m. (pl.): Name of a people. A. Location: To the south of Indra-prastha (प्रययौ दक्षिणां दिशम्) 2. 28 1; (दक्षिणाभिमुखो ययौ) 2. 28. 8; (प्रायाद्  … दक्षिणां दिशम्) 2. 28. 37. B. Epic event: Sahadeva, in his expedition before the Rājasūya, subjugated them just by sending envoys and made them pay tribute (कलिङ्गान् ओष्ट्रकर्णिकान् । … दूतैर् एव वशे चक्रे करं चैनान् अदापयत्) 2. 28. 48-49. [Identical with the preceding ?]
